questions.text:
There are two enantiomers (optical isomers) of galactose, called D-galactose and L-galactose.

Label all the asymmetric carbon atoms with an asterisk (*) in the open-chain structural formula of D-galactose shown below.

CHO-C(H)(OH)-C(H)(OH)-C(H)(OH)-C(H)(OH)-CH2OH
(C1 = CHO, C6 = CH2OH)
questions.expectedAnswer: There are FOUR asymmetric (chiral) carbon atoms in the open-chain form of D-galactose: C-2, C-3, C-4, and C-5. Each of these carbons is bonded to four different groups. C-1 (CHO) and C-6 (CH2OH) are not chiral.

questions.text: Explain how D-galactose and L-galactose could be distinguished.
questions.expectedAnswer: The enantiomers can be distinguished using a polarimeter. They rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises rotation of plane-polarised light.

For Merit:
- Explains opposite directions.

questions.text:
When D-galactose is heated with Tollens' reagent, a silver mirror forms.

Explain this observation with reference to the functional group involved and the type of reaction occurring.
questions.expectedAnswer: D-galactose is an aldose (aldohexose) — its open-chain form contains an aldehyde (-CHO) group on C1. Tollens' reagent oxidises the aldehyde to a carboxylate ion, while Ag+ in Tollens' is reduced to metallic silver, which deposits as a silver mirror on the inside of the test tube. This is a redox reaction and shows that D-galactose is a reducing sugar.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies oxidation or reducing sugar.

For Merit:
- Explains the reaction.

questions.text:
Devise a reaction scheme to convert hexanal into N-hexylhexanamide.

CH3-(CH2)4-C(=O)-N(H)-(CH2)5-CH3   (N-hexylhexanamide)

Assume that you are provided only with the following reagents:
SOCl2, Cr2O72-/H+, NaBH4, conc NH3 (reagents can be used more than once).
questions.expectedAnswer: Path 1 (to the acyl chloride): hexanal + Cr2O72-/H+ with heat -> hexanoic acid; then hexanoic acid + SOCl2 -> hexanoyl chloride. Path 2 (to the primary amine): hexanal + NaBH4 -> hexan-1-ol; then hexan-1-ol + SOCl2 -> 1-chlorohexane; then 1-chlorohexane + excess concentrated NH3 -> hexan-1-amine. Final step: hexanoyl chloride + hexan-1-amine -> N-hexylhexanamide (amide formation).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- At least TWO steps correct.

For Merit:
- At least FOUR steps.

For Excellence:
- ALL correct.

questions.text:
A student wanted to make some hexanal, CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2CHO. The student heated some hexan-1-ol and excess acidified potassium permanganate, KMnO4/H+, under reflux for 20 minutes, then distilled. However, no fraction was collected at 127-131 degrees C.

Describe the colour change observed, and link it to the type of reaction.
questions.expectedAnswer: Purple to colourless (or brown). This is an oxidation reaction.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct colour change and reaction type.

questions.text:
Explain why no fraction was collected at 127-131 degrees C.

The boiling points of the relevant compounds are shown in the graph above.

graph.title: Boiling Points of Compounds in the Reaction

questions.expectedAnswer: The hexan-1-ol was fully oxidised past the aldehyde stage to hexanoic acid because excess oxidising agent and reflux were used. Hexanoic acid has bp 205 degrees C, much higher than 129 degrees C.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises over-oxidation to carboxylic acid.

For Merit:
- Explains why no fraction at 127-131 degrees C (the hexanal was all further oxidised to hexanoic acid which has a much higher boiling point).

questions.text:
Outline why the student should have used distillation instead of reflux to produce hexanal.

Include an explanation of the process of distillation and compare the position of the condenser between distillation and reflux.
questions.expectedAnswer: Distillation removes the hexanal from the reaction mixture as soon as it forms, preventing further oxidation. In distillation the condenser is angled downward to collect distillate, while in reflux it is vertical to return vapours.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises distillation removes product.

For Merit:
- Explains how distillation prevents over-oxidation.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation with condenser comparison.

questions.text:
Complete the table above by naming or drawing the structural formula.

Compound A: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CH3 -> IUPAC name?
Compound B: -> structural formula for pentyl ethanoate
Compound C: -> structural formula for 4-methylheptanamide
Compound D: CH3-CH(Cl)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-H -> IUPAC name?
questions.expectedAnswer: A (CH3(CH2)4C(=O)CH3): heptan-2-one. B (pentyl ethanoate): CH3-C(=O)-O-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH3. C (4-methylheptanamide): H2N-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH3. D (CH3CH(Cl)CH2CH2CHO): 4-chloropentanal.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- THREE correct.

For Merit:
- ALL four correct.

questions.text: Draw the enantiomers (optical isomers) of Compound D.
questions.expectedAnswer: Two 3D structural drawings of 4-chloropentanal showing the four different groups (CH3, Cl, H, -CH2CH2CHO) arranged as non-superimposable mirror images around the asymmetric C4.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Shows tetrahedral arrangement.

For Merit:
- Enantiomers correctly drawn.

questions.text:
Three bottles, each containing a different colourless liquid, have not been labelled. They are:
- butan-1-ol  - butanoyl chloride  - butanal

A student devised the following procedure:

Step 1: Add water to all three.
Step 2: Add Fehling's solution to the remaining two, and heat.
Step 3: Add acidified potassium dichromate to the remaining one, and heat.

Complete the table for each step, only including observations for reactions that occur.
questions.expectedAnswer: Step 1: Butanoyl chloride reacts vigorously with water, producing steamy fumes of HCl (identifies butanoyl chloride). Step 2: Butanal reduces Fehling's solution on heating, giving a brick-red (orange-red) precipitate of Cu2O (identifies butanal). Step 3: Butan-1-ol is oxidised by acidified dichromate on heating, with an orange-to-green colour change (identifies butan-1-ol).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE row correct.

For Merit:
- TWO rows correct.

questions.text: Justify why the three steps should be followed in the order given.
questions.expectedAnswer: Water must be added first because butanoyl chloride reacts violently and would interfere with other tests. Fehling's is used next because it specifically tests for aldehydes. Dichromate last as it is less specific.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE point correct.

For Merit:
- THREE points.

For Excellence:
- FIVE points.

questions.text:
Compound A has molecular formula C4H8O2 and exists as enantiomers. When dilute sulfuric acid is added, two organic compounds form: Compound B (higher proportion) and Compound C. Compound B is reacted with SOCl2 then conc NH3 to form Compound D (turns red litmus blue). Compound C is heated with excess acidified KMnO4 to form Compound E (bubbles with Na2CO3).

Draw the structural formulae for Compounds A, B, C, D, and E.
questions.expectedAnswer: A is an ester with a chiral centre (e.g. methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate or similar C4H8O2 ester). B is the carboxylic acid. C is the alcohol. D is the amide. E is a carboxylic acid from alcohol oxidation.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- ONE correct functional group for A, D, E AND TWO correct structures.

For Merit:
- THREE correct.

For Excellence:
- ALL correct.

questions.text:
Using the following two amino acids, draw the structural formulae for the two possible dipeptides.

Amino acid 1: H2N-CH(CH3)-COOH (alanine)
Amino acid 2: H2N-CH(CH2OH)-COOH (serine)
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Draws an amide linkage.

For Merit:
- Both dipeptides correct.

questions.text: Identify and explain the type of reaction occurring to form the two dipeptides.
questions.expectedAnswer: This is a condensation reaction. An amide (peptide) bond is formed between the -NH2 group of one amino acid and the -COOH group of another, with loss of a water molecule.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies condensation.

For Merit:
- Explains with amide bond and loss of water.

questions.text:
Nylon 6,6 is a polymer used in the textiles industry. Two repeating units of nylon 6,6 are shown:

-[NH-(CH2)6-NH-CO-(CH2)4-CO]2-

Circle ONE amide linkage in the above diagram of nylon 6,6.

Identify and explain the type of reaction that would occur when nylon 6,6 is heated under reflux with hydrochloric acid, HCl, solution.

Draw the structural formulae of the organic products.
questions.expectedAnswer: Acidic hydrolysis occurs. The amide linkages are broken by water in the presence of acid, regenerating the diamine and dicarboxylic acid monomers.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Identifies hydrolysis.

For Merit:
- TWO correct products.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation with products.

questions.text:
Consider compounds W, X, and Y:

Compound W: CH3-CH2-CH=CH-C(=O)-H
Compound X: CH2=CH-CH2-CH2-COOH
Compound Y: CH3-C(=O)-CH=CH-COOH

Identify the ONE compound that has ALL the following properties:
- exists as cis-trans isomers
- reacts with thionyl chloride, SOCl2, to produce steamy fumes
- can be reduced by sodium borohydride, NaBH4.

Explain your choice.
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound Y. It has a C=C with different groups each side (cis-trans), a -COOH group (reacts with SOCl2), and a C=O ketone group (reduced by NaBH4).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Recognises at least one property for two compounds.

For Merit:
- Chooses Y with two properties.

For Excellence:
- Full explanation including elimination of others.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional isomer of C5H9O3Br (Compound S) that has:
- a secondary alcohol group
- a carboxylic acid group.
questions.expectedAnswer: An example: HOOC-CH2-CH(Br)-CH(OH)-CH3 (3-bromo-2-hydroxypentanoic acid numbered from COOH as C1... or 3-bromo-4-hydroxypentanoic acid depending on numbering). Formula C5H9BrO3. It has a carboxylic acid group at one end (-COOH), a secondary -OH on the carbon bonded to CH3, and a Br on the adjacent carbon.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Draws one functional group.

For Merit:
- Both functional groups correct.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional isomer of C5H9Cl (Compound T) that has:
- a branched chain
- a C=C double bond
- an asymmetric carbon atom.
questions.expectedAnswer: 3-chloro-2-methylbut-1-ene: CH2=C(CH3)-CH(Cl)-CH3. Formula C5H9Cl. It has a methyl branch on C2 (branched chain), a C=C double bond between C1 and C2, and an asymmetric (chiral) carbon at C3 bonded to four different groups (-CH=C(CH3)-, -CH3, -H, -Cl).
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Draws a branched chain or C=C.

For Merit:
- All three features.

For Excellence:
- Correct formula.
